title: What does XChainClaim do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of XChainClaim and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, XChainClaim collects committed value on a bridge's destination chain when the claim requirements are met. [1]

The claim refers to the configured bridge and claim identifier, with destination and authorization rules. Source commitment, witness attestations and destination delivery are distinct stages. Inspect the successful destination transaction before crediting the beneficiary. This transaction does not remove the bridge's reliance on its selected witnesses and operating assumptions. [1]

The XChainClaim reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using XChainClaim, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
